criteria.title: Scope: cross-cutting policy, never business logic

levels.0: Lists 'routing and auth' only, or happily puts response aggregation and product rules into the gateway.
levels.1: Covers auth, routing, rate limits and quotas, but never says what the gateway must not do, or misses metering and live config changes.
levels.2: Covers authN/authZ offload, routing by path and version, limits and quotas, transformation, upstream protection, metering and live config, and explicitly rejects aggregation as a BFF's job.

criteria.title: Non-functional targets that follow from being in series with everything

levels.0: No latency, availability or isolation targets.
levels.1: States 10 ms and high availability but not why the gateway must beat its upstreams, or omits isolation between routes.
levels.2: 10 ms p99 gateway-only budget, 99.99% because availability multiplies in series, per-route isolation, config propagation in seconds, and billing accuracy separated from quota-enforcement lag.

levels.0: No instance count, or 500k ÷ per-instance capacity with no headroom.
levels.1: Computes average and per-region load and an instance count, but does not check utilisation with a zone or a region lost.
levels.2: 200k average, 167k per region at peak, 10k per instance as a labelled assumption, 36 per region in 3 AZs, ρ 0.46 / 0.70 (AZ lost) / 0.69 (region lost), and names the double failure it does not provision for.

levels.1: Does a latency budget or limiter sizing, but does not connect a number to a decision.
levels.2: Itemised ~1 ms latency budget, IdP at 500k vs 5,000/s (100×) forcing local validation, Redis shards sized by ops/s not memory, and usage aggregation cutting 150 MB/s of events to ~32k rows/s.

levels.1: Shows the forwarded request or a 429, but not identity headers, spoofing protection or the config API.
levels.2: Forwarded request with request ID, tenant, scopes, deadline and trace headers; stripping of client-supplied identity headers; 429 with Retry-After distinguishing rate limit from quota; config API with If-Match and an honest 202 rollout status.

levels.0: One database for everything, or none.
levels.1: Picks stores for config and counters, but stores plaintext keys or puts the config database on the request path.
levels.2: Postgres for versioned, audited config (hashed keys only); per-region, unpersisted Redis counters with hash tags; aggregated usage via Kafka to a columnar store with (instance, flush_seq) dedup; endpoints pushed, never queried per request.

levels.0: A box labelled 'gateway' between clients and services.
levels.1: Shows LB, gateways and upstreams, but the per-request steps or the config and usage paths are missing.
levels.2: GeoDNS to three regions, L4 LB over gateways in three AZs, the ordered per-request steps (route, auth, quota flag, limit, transform, forward, meter), plus the write, over-limit, config-change and usage paths.

levels.0: Calls the IdP per request, or validates only the signature.
levels.1: Validates JWTs locally but ignores rotation, unknown kid handling or revocation.
levels.2: Local validation with pinned algorithms and full claim checks; short TTL plus pushed jti denylist; JWKS refreshed in background, last-good kept, single-flight and rate-limited refresh on unknown kid; fails closed on signatures.

levels.0: Per-instance limits only, or a database counter per request.
levels.1: Central Redis counter with Lua, but no plan for hot tenants, regions or Redis failure.
levels.2: Token bucket per tenant in Redis via Lua; token leases for hot tenants; per-region counters with the slack stated; fail open or closed chosen per limit class with a 3 ms timeout; quotas enforced asynchronously with the overshoot bounded (about 0.12%).

criteria.title: Timeouts, retries, circuit breaking and isolation

levels.1: Timeouts, retries and a breaker, but retries are unbounded or applied to non-idempotent writes, and there is no concurrency cap.
levels.2: Uses Little's law to show how one slow upstream exhausts shared capacity; per-upstream concurrency caps, deadline propagation, idempotent-only retries within a budget, outlier ejection and breakers; a second-by-second failure timeline.

levels.0: Gateways read routes from the database on each request or are restarted to pick up changes.
levels.1: Pushes config but rolls it out to everyone at once, or has no last-known-good behaviour.
levels.2: Control/data plane split, versioned snapshots with ACK/NACK, validation including linear-time regex, staged rollout with auto-rollback, atomic swap, and a guard against discovery deltas that remove most endpoints.

levels.0: Does not consider the gateway itself failing or adding latency.
levels.1: Makes the gateway redundant but never discusses when not to use one or what breaks at 10×.
levels.2: Stateless N+1 per AZ and region, no hot-path dependency weaker than the gateway, priority shedding; explains the latency tax and hairpinning, BFF vs single gateway vs none; at 10× names the limiter store, key table, config fan-out and cells/shuffle sharding.
